name: Pleuro-pericardial cyst

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiologic and clinical diagnostic criteria for pleuro-pericardial cyst

criteria.description: Identification of a well-defined, fluid-filled cyst adjacent to the pericardium on chest imaging (CT or MRI)
No solid or enhancing components within the cyst on imaging studies
Clinical presentation consistent with pleuro-pericardial cyst such as chest discomfort or incidental finding in asymptomatic patient

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cystic lesion on imaging with absence of solid components; clinical correlation supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis may require histopathological confirmation if surgical resection is performed

pathognomonic.notes: Most cases are discovered incidentally on imaging
searchTerms: incidentally found chest cyst without symptoms

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized chest discomfort related to cyst compression
pathognomonic.notes: Mild chest pain or pressure due to cyst size or location
searchTerms: localized chest pain due to cyst
pain from cyst compressing chest structures

common.notes: Due to compression of adjacent lung tissue
Occasional cardiac arrhythmias from cyst pressure

occasional.notes: Rarely auscultated if cyst irritates pericardium

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to nerve pressure
trouble swallowing due to food pipe blockage

occasional.notes: Rarely palpable if cyst is large and anterior

rare.notes: Extremely rare complication due to cyst rupture or hemorrhage

rare.symptomName: Infection of cyst leading to mediastinitis
searchTerms: cyst infection leading to chest inflammation
abnormal heart rhythms managed by doctors

laboratory: Typically normal laboratory studies; no specific biomarkers
imaging: Well-circumscribed, fluid-attenuation cyst adjacent to pericardium on chest CT
MRI showing homogenous cystic lesion without solid components or enhancement
Chest X-ray may show mediastinal mass
other: Histopathology shows cyst lined by mesothelial cells if resected

distinguishingFeatures: May contain mucous or air-fluid levels
Fluid accumulation in pericardial sac without cyst wall
Dynamic changes with position and cardiac cycle
Associated with systemic diseases or infections
May have septations or solid components

redFlags: Sudden onset chest pain with hemodynamic instability
Rapid increase in cyst size or symptoms suggestive of infection or hemorrhage
references: Kumar V, Abbas AK, Aster JC. Robbins Basic Pathology. 10th Edition. Elsevier; 2018.
Mediastinal cysts: Clinical and radiologic features. Radiographics. 2017;37(3): 1003-1019.
